# amux

> amux (amux.io, github.com/mixpeek/amux) is the agent control plane, made by Mixpeek. It runs dozens of AI coding agents in parallel (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and Ollama-backed local models) and lets you control them from a web dashboard (installable PWA), a native iPhone and iPad app, or a native Mac app. Self-host it free on macOS or Linux, or run it on amux Cloud. License: MIT + Commons Clause (source-available).

amux is a single Rust binary with SQLite storage. Each agent runs as a real, unmodified CLI session in tmux. Agents share a task board with atomic claiming, so two agents never take the same task; they message each other, run on schedules and loops, and amux resumes them after usage limits; on macOS every worker comes back in its own conversation after a reboot. From your phone you can steer a session, approve actions and answer blocked prompts. Outbound email from agents waits for owner approval, and browser automation uses saved sign-in profiles. Updated October 2026.

Not to be confused with amux.sh or github.com/andyrewlee/amux: those are different projects and are not affiliated with amux.io.

## Quick Start

Install with one command (macOS or Linux):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://amux.io/install.sh | bash
# then open https://localhost:8824
```

From source: `git clone https://github.com/mixpeek/amux && cd amux && ./install.sh`. Requirements: tmux 3.2+ and at least one agent CLI. There is no Python server; the Homebrew and PyPI packages are retired.

## Platforms

- Web dashboard, installable as a PWA (Android and any browser)
- Native iPhone and iPad app (one app for both): https://apps.apple.com/us/app/amux-agent-multiplexer/id6760410435
- Native macOS app (macOS 12+, Apple silicon and Intel, not notarized yet): https://github.com/mixpeek/amux/releases/download/desktop-latest/Amux-macOS.dmg
- Every app connects to your own amux server or your amux Cloud address.

## Agents and providers

- Claude Code, Codex (OpenAI Codex CLI), Gemini CLI, OpenCode and Ollama-backed local models, side by side in one fleet
- Switch a worker's model or provider while it runs
- amux reads agent status from structured hook events where the agent provides them, and from the terminal otherwise

## Hosting

- Self-host: free on your own Mac or Linux machine; no account needed.
- amux Cloud: your own dedicated, always-on amux server at yourname.amux.io. Solo $39/mo (4 vCPU, 8 GB), Team $69/mo (8 vCPU, 16 GB), Max $129/mo (16 vCPU, 32 GB). Bring your Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini account, or an API key. Start: https://amux.io/start/
- Move a local setup to Cloud: `amux export`, then `amux import <file> --to https://<you>.amux.io`.
- Model costs are paid to your model provider and depend on your provider plan.

You may not sell amux itself, meaning provide to third parties, for a fee, a product or service whose value derives entirely or substantially from amux. By the OSI definition this is source-available, not OSI-approved open source.

## Security and remote access

- API and dashboard access needs a bearer token minted at `~/.amux/auth_token`; localhost callers are exempt. Cross-site requests are refused.
- Never expose port 8824 to the public internet. Use Tailscale for remote access: no public ports and no SSH exposure needed.
- Tailscale setup: install Tailscale on the server and your devices (same tailnet); run `tailscale cert` for the server's ts.net name with the cert and key written to `~/.amux/tls/` (enable HTTPS certificates in the Tailscale admin console); restart amux; open `https://<host>.<tailnet>.ts.net:8824` or add that URL in the iOS or Mac app. amux serves that certificate for the ts.net name and keeps its self-signed certificate for localhost. Re-run `tailscale cert` before the 90-day expiry.
- Optional: `AMUX_TRUST_TAILNET_OWNER=1` signs in the owner's own tailnet devices automatically; `AMUX_TAILNET_MEMBER_AUTH=1` lets invited tailnet members sign in by Tailscale login, and removal from the tailnet revokes access within a minute.
- amux Cloud servers can join your tailnet from the dashboard; nothing about your tailnet passes through amux Cloud.
- Guide: https://amux.io/guides/remote-access-tailscale/

## How amux differs from plain Claude Code

Claude Code runs one agent per terminal. amux runs dozens of agents from several CLIs, with live monitoring, phone and desktop apps, recovery from usage limits and reboots, and a shared task board. amux does not modify or patch the agent CLIs; it runs them as real sessions in tmux.

## Documentation

- [Documentation](https://amux.io/docs/): Reference for amux: installation, CLI commands, web dashboard, REST API (sessions, board, notes, CRM, email, browser, scheduler), kanban board with atomic task claiming, notes, CRM, email with owner approval for outbound sends, browser automation with saved sign-in profiles, scheduler, skills and slash commands, inter-session messaging, recovery (usage limits, restarts, reboots), PWA and mobile apps, authentication, TLS/HTTPS, configuration and architecture.

- [Security: what amux can and cannot access](https://amux.io/security/): Self-hosted amux sends nothing to amux. amux Cloud gives each customer a dedicated Hetzner server (Germany or Finland); code, prompts, files and model keys stay on it. Stripe Checkout takes payment; the password is scrypt-hashed in the browser. Firewall allows 22, 80, 443; a sign-in gate with Let's Encrypt TLS fronts everything. What the team can reach: the Hetzner console and snapshots, two-minute sign-in links (Sign in with Apple), and an hourly usage report of counts only. Deletion erases server, backups and snapshots at once; canceling keeps a snapshot 30 days. No certifications or audits claimed.

- [amux Is a Graph — Task Dependencies, Agent Edges and Fleet Topology (2026)](https://amux.io/guides/ai-agent-graph/): amux models every aspect of a parallel AI agent fleet as two interlocking graphs. Task graph: board cards are nodes; depends_on edges create a DAG (prerequisite gates enforced atomically at claim time — if dependency is not done, /claim returns 409); reviewer edges create completion gates (node cannot reach verified until named reviewer clears it); status is the node state machine (todo → doing → done → verified). Session graph: running agent sessions are nodes; POST /api/sessions/NAME/send creates directed instruction edges; GET /api/sessions/NAME/peek creates observation edges; channels create bidirectional persistent edges. Four coordination patterns covered: fan-out (independent parallel root nodes), pipeline (A→B→C sequential), diamond (parallel B+C merge at D), hub-and-spoke (orchestrator builds graph, workers traverse). Automatic prompt decomposition creates one node per task. Complete graph API reference (add node, add edge, traverse, advance state, read graph). ## Features

- [Recovery: What amux Does When AI Agents Stop (2026)](https://amux.io/features/self-healing/): amux keeps agents going through usage limits and restarts: delivery is held and resumes at the provider's reset, the OS service (launchd or systemd) restarts the amux server, on macOS every non-archived worker comes back in its own conversation after a reboot, Claude Code compacts its own context at a threshold you set in amux, and stall detection fires owner alerts. Restarting a crashed agent process is not built into the server; an optional macOS script restarts crashed Claude Code workers and is not installed by default.
- [AI Agent Dashboard — amux Web Dashboard & iOS App (2026)](https://amux.io/features/web-dashboard/): The amux dashboard covers sessions (live status dots, token spend, plan strip), peek panel (SSE-streamed terminal output, subagent switcher ▲/▼, load earlier output scrollback, steering bar), board (SQLite kanban with atomic CAS claiming), notes, CRM, scheduler, and calendar. Mobile: native iOS app (id6760410435) + PWA. SSE backbone — all clients see changes within ~2s. Comparison table vs DIY tmux / Claude Code alone / Devin (7 capabilities). FAQPage JSON-LD (5 Qs). Updated July 2026.
- [AI Agent Coordination — amux REST API & Atomic Task Claiming (2026)](https://amux.io/features/agent-coordination/): Every amux session gets $AMUX_URL and $AMUX_SESSION at startup. Coordination primitives: atomic SQLite CAS board claim (POST /api/board/:id/claim — 200 if won, 409 if taken), inter-session messaging (POST /api/sessions/:name/send), peer output reading (GET /api/sessions/:name/peek), global memory, and agent discovery (GET /api/sessions). Common patterns: producer-consumer, pipeline, role-based routing. Comparison table vs LangGraph/file-based/Redis (5 approaches). FAQPage JSON-LD (5 Qs). Updated July 2026.
- [Mobile PWA & iOS App — Manage AI Agents from Your Phone (2026)](https://amux.io/features/mobile-pwa/): Native iOS app (App Store id6760410435) + installable PWA for Android. Full dashboard on 375px screen: fleet scan, peek panel, plan strip, subagent switcher, load earlier output, steering bar, board, notes, CRM, scheduler. Touch targets ≥44×44px, safe-area-inset-* for iOS notch, responsive peek reflows to phone width. Offline queue via Background Sync. Remote access: Tailscale (recommended) or amux Cloud. Comparison table: iOS app vs PWA vs SSH+tmux vs Devin mobile. FAQPage JSON-LD (5 Qs). Updated July 2026.
- [Rust Workspace Architecture — How amux is Built (2026)](https://amux.io/features/single-file-architecture/): amux is a 4-crate Cargo workspace (amux-server, amux-dashboard, amux-core, amux-cli) that compiles to a single binary. The dashboard is real static files (app.js, app.css, index.html, sw.js) in amux-dashboard/static/ — no inline HTML. A background build watcher rebuilds on every commit; the running server self-adopts (exits cleanly, launchd restarts) without manual intervention. No Docker, no config files, no external service dependencies beyond tmux. MIT + Commons Clause. Deployment: one binary install via install.sh. Contributing: clone the workspace, cargo check, commit — the auto-builder ships it.
- [amux Cloud: your own amux server, running 24/7](https://amux.io/cloud/): amux Cloud is your own dedicated amux server at yourname.amux.io. Workers keep running when your laptop sleeps, and you sign in from any browser or the iOS app. Same product as the open-source install; we run the box. Plans: Solo $39/mo, Team $69/mo, Max $129/mo, billed monthly. Move an existing install with amux export, then amux import <file> --to https://<you>.amux.io. Start at https://amux.io/start/.

## Comparisons

- [amux vs Hermes Agent](https://amux.io/compare/amux-vs-hermes-agent/): NousResearch's open-source self-improving personal AI daemon (175k GitHub stars, Feb 2026) vs amux parallel coding fleet. Hermes = single persistent agent with cross-session memory, skill self-improvement, 16+ messaging platform connectors, any LLM including local. amux = 10-50 parallel coding agents (Claude Code/Codex/Gemini CLI), shared kanban with atomic claiming, overnight runs that resume after usage limits, mobile fleet management. Different jobs: depth for one agent vs throughput for many. FAQPage JSON-LD (5 Qs). July 2026.
- [amux vs Cowork](https://amux.io/compare/amux-vs-cowork/): Claude Cowork (Anthropic's single computer-use agent, available on paid Claude plans) vs amux (parallel coding fleet, open source). Cowork = one agent, GUI/computer-use tasks, desktop app, Claude only. amux = unlimited parallel sessions, coding-agent specific (Claude Code/Codex/Gemini CLI), usage-limit resume, mobile management, free + API tokens. Throughput comparison: 20 tasks in 1hr (10 parallel amux sessions) vs 10hr (Cowork sequential). FAQPage JSON-LD (5 Qs). July 2026.
- [amux vs OpenClaw](https://amux.io/compare/amux-vs-openclaw/): OpenClaw (formerly Warelay/Moltbot, 347k GitHub stars — most starred repo in history, MIT, OpenAI-backed) vs amux. OpenClaw = messaging-native personal assistant (WhatsApp/Telegram/Slack/Discord/iMessage/20+ more), 100+ AgentSkills, low technical floor, single agent. amux = developer fleet dashboard (web PWA + iOS app), parallel coding agents, kanban coordination, git-safe worktrees, overnight usage-limit resume. Complementary tools for different audiences. FAQPage JSON-LD (5 Qs). July 2026.
- [amux vs Claude Managed Agents](https://amux.io/compare/amux-vs-claude-managed-agents/): Self-hosted alternative to Anthropic's April 2026 Managed Agents launch. $0 session fees vs $0.08/session-hour, model-agnostic, MIT-licensed.
- [amux vs Claude Code Agent Teams — parallel fleet vs sub-task fan-out (2026)](https://amux.io/compare/amux-vs-claude-code-agent-teams/): Accurate comparison of amux and Anthropic's experimental Claude Code Agent Teams (requires CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1, Claude Code v2.1.32+). Agent Teams = parent session spawns sub-agents with git worktree isolation, great for tightly-coupled sub-task fan-out. amux = independent long-running fleet sessions with usage-limit resume, web dashboard, mobile PWA, shared kanban, CRM/email/browser, multi-runtime (Claude Code + Codex + Gemini CLI). 17-row comparison table. "Why not both?" section explains how the two compose. BreadcrumbList + Article + FAQPage JSON-LD (5 Qs). Updated July 2026.
- [amux vs Continue.dev (2026): AI Agent Team vs AI Coding Assistant](https://amux.io/compare/amux-vs-continue/): Continue.dev (Apache 2.0, VS Code / JetBrains extension, supports Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini/Ollama and more via config.json) vs amux (MIT+CC, open-source control plane for parallel autonomous AI coding agents). Continue.dev = IDE AI assistant for interactive coding with inline completions and chat. amux = unattended overnight agent runs, 10-100 parallel sessions, usage-limit resume, mobile dashboard. Complementary tools: Continue.dev while you code, amux while you sleep. 13-row comparison table. FAQPage JSON-LD (6 Qs). Article + BreadcrumbList JSON-LD. EXP-096 CTA. September 2026.

Eliminates shared-checkout conflicts between parallel Claude Code agents — dirty-tree failures, read-race wrong conclusions, last-write-wins clobbers, and staged-index collisions. - [Agent Multiplexer — Glossary](https://amux.io/glossary/agent-multiplexer/): Full definition of "agent multiplexer" — a platform that runs and monitors dozens of parallel AI coding agents from one dashboard. Covers how it works (tmux sessions + status detection + REST API), comparison table (raw tmux vs shell scripts vs agent multiplexer across 8 capabilities), 6-question FAQ (FAQPage JSON-LD), Article + DefinedTerm + BreadcrumbList JSON-LD. Distinguishes multiplexers from task queues: task queues are stateless; agent multiplexers are stateful (sessions hold context across tasks). amux is the open-source reference implementation. Updated August 2026 with comparison table, FAQ, and EXP-051 CTA.
- [AI Agent Fleet — Glossary](https://amux.io/glossary/ai-agent-fleet/): Full definition of "AI agent fleet" — a coordinated group of AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI) running concurrently under a shared orchestration layer. Covers fleet components (agent sessions/tmux, task queue/kanban, usage-limit resume, SSE monitoring dashboard), fleet vs single-agent vs orchestrator vs task queue comparison table (5-row), fleet sizing (200-400 MB per agent), multi-runtime fleets, and how amux manages fleets (session cloning, age-weighted pickup, GitHub App token shim, SSE health signal). DefinedTerm + Article + BreadcrumbList + FAQPage JSON-LD (6 Qs). EXP-065 CTA. New August 2026.
- [AI Agent Control Plane — Glossary](https://amux.io/glossary/ai-agent-control-plane/): Full definition of "AI agent control plane" — the infrastructure layer that manages lifecycle, health, task routing, credential scoping, and recovery for a fleet of AI coding agents. Distinguishes control planes from orchestrators (orchestrators sequence workflows; control planes manage the infrastructure of agents themselves) and task queues (stateless vs stateful). Covers the 6 things a control plane manages: session lifecycle, health/recovery, task routing (kanban board), credential scoping (OAuth broker), observability (dashboard + iOS app + REST API), and scheduling. 3-column comparison table (task queue vs orchestrator vs control plane), 6-question FAQ (FAQPage JSON-LD), DefinedTerm + Article + BreadcrumbList JSON-LD. amux is the open-source reference implementation. New August 2026 with EXP-052 CTA.
